framework.name: Inclusive economic development, with a focus on employment and social protection

children.name: Outcome 1.1 - Outcome 1: By 2020, equitable and sustainable economic growth through productive employment, improvement of environment for business, entrepreneurship and innovations expanded for all.
children.description:
The overarching goal of this Outcome is to promote inclusive growth and human development, with a focus on vulnerable groups and regions.To galvanize the inter-linkages needed between comprehensive development strategies that guide the development process, effective employment policies, and the role of the enabling environment for private sector development to expand productive employment opportunities, the following aspects thus will be prioritized:
a) Further strengthening national capacities for formulation and implementation of comprehensive development strategies and policies
b) Improving the business environment
c) Promoting productive and sustainable employment opportunities for vulnerable groups, with a special focus on youth and women
d) Further addressing regional development disparities
e) Enhancing national systems for protection and support of labour migrants

projects.description:
"In 2020, the project provided FFS trainings on various improved agricultural and apicultural practices for a total of 152 smallholders including 87 females and 65 males, i.e. 43% being rural women within Central Asian Desert Initiative (CADI) project. Through these trainings, smallholders learned how to better adapt to the changing climate by introducing cold tolerant crop varieties and establishment of tree nurseries in greenhouses. The benefits of beekeeping explained during FFS sessions include pollination services that largely contribute to supporting of ecosystems and biodiversity conservation. 
In 2020, six online training courses were conducted on Sustainable Land Management practices. The online training courses brought together the representatives from Research Institutes and and Universities in the agricultural sector and having diverse background (Agronomy, Soils, Breeding and Water Management). A total number of 326 participants attended the online training courses including 49 women within Integrated natural resources management in drought-prone and salt-affected agricultural production landscapes in Central Asia and Turkey ('CACILM2') project"

projects.description:
During the reporting period, Risk Communication and Community Engagement activities were broadly grouped into following three phases of COVID-19 response, namely (1) early response, (2) critical response and early recover, (3) early recovery and continued response. 
At early response stage communication products focused on ensuring that people (children, parents/care givers, pregnant women and their families, at risk groups) have the life-saving information they need to protect themselves and others. Communication materials at the second stage focused on increasing the coping skills and resilience of children, adolescents and parents.
Overall, more than 80 communication products, including videos, animations, posters, TV shows, were developed in 2020. The reach through Telegram messenger only was over 6,6 mln. people.

projects.name: 2.1.2.6 - Assessment and building capacities in planning, procurement and logistics in Immunization
projects.description:
UNICEF developed a unified methodology and tool for vaccine procurement budgeting and forecasting for the development of comprehensive annual budgets, and another methodology and tool for cold chain maintenance budgeting, including full cold chain inventory system. National partners were trained to use the provided tools.
UNICEF supported project on development and introduction of a comprehensive, precise and professional quality monitoring system - Vaccine Logistics Management Information System (VLMIS). The VLMIS will connect all cold chain stores located at various levels into one network for constant consolidation and analysis of up-to-date information on vaccines stock, its movement and consumption, and possible re-fill, will provide a ready-to-go reports and information for decision makers, serve as a basis for the budgeting and forecasting. In coordination with national and international counterparts, UNICEF developed TOR and contracted an international IT company to develop VLMIS. The first pilot version of VLMIS will be ready in April 2021, with gradual expansion to cover all cold-chain stores in the country.
UNICEF provided technical assistance for the optimization of current vaccination and stock monitoring reports in order to provide effective data for management and taking key decisions. New reporting tool with dashboard visualization has been developed, presented to national partners, and currently under review process.
